readings.subsection: God Challenges Job from the Whirlwind
readings.title: Where Were You?
readings.subtitle: The Foundations of the Earth
readings.text: [Job 38:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered <dn>את</dn> Job out of the whirlwind, and said: [2] <dq>“Who is this who darkens counsel By words without knowledge?</dq> [3] <dq>Now gird up your loins like a man; And <dn>I</dn> ask you, and you answer <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [4] <dq>Where were you when <dn>I</dn> laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.</dq> [5] <dq>Who set its measurements, if you know? Or who stretched the line upon it?</dq> [6] <dq>Upon what were its foundations sunk? Or who laid its cornerstone,</dq> [7] <dq>When the morning stars sang together, And all the sons of <dn>Elohim</dn> shouted for joy?</dq> [8] <dq>Or who shut in the sea with doors, When it burst forth and issued from the womb;</dq> [9] <dq>When <dn>I</dn> made the clouds its garment, And thick darkness its swaddling band;</dq> [10] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> established <dn>My</dn> limit for it, And set bars and doors;</dq> [11] <dq>And said, ‘This far you come, but no further, And here your proud waves are stopped’?</dq> [12] <dq>Have you commanded the morning since your days began, And caused the dawn to know its place,</dq> [13] <dq>To take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wrong be shaken out of it?</dq> [14] <dq>It is changed like clay under a seal, And they stand out like a garment.</dq> [15] <dq>And from the wrong their light is withheld, And the upraised arm is broken.</dq> [16] <dq>Have you entered the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in search of the depths?</dq> [17] <dq>Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the doors of the shadow of death?</dq> [18] <dq>Have you understood the breadth of the earth? Declare, if you know it all.</dq>

readings.title: The Mysteries of the Heavens
readings.subtitle: Light, Snow, and Stars
readings.text: [Job 38:19] <dq>“Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And darkness, where is its place,</dq> [20] <dq>That you should take it to its boundary, And know the paths to its home?</dq> [21] <dq>Do you know it, because you were born then, Or because the number of your days is great?</dq> [22] <dq>Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, Or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,</dq> [23] <dq>Which <dn>I</dn> have reserved for the time of distress, For the day of fighting and battle?</dq> [24] <dq>Where is the way that light is divided, Or the east wind scattered over the earth?</dq> [25] <dq>Who has cleft a channel for the overflowing water, Or a way for the lightning of thunder,</dq> [26] <dq>To cause it to rain on the earth where no one is, On the wilderness in which there is no man;</dq> [27] <dq>To satisfy the wild and waste places, And to cause the sprout of grass to spring forth?</dq> [28] <dq>Does the rain have a father? Or who has brought forth the drops of dew?</dq> [29] <dq>From whose womb comes the ice? And the frost of the heavens, who gives it birth?</dq> [30] <dq>The waters harden like stone, And the face of the deep is frozen.</dq> [31] <dq>Do you bind the bands of Kimah, Or loosen the cords of Kesil?</dq> [32] <dq>Do you bring out Mazzaroth in its season? Or do you lead Ayish with her sons?</dq> [33] <dq>Do you know the laws of the heavens? Or do you set their rule over the earth?</dq> [34] <dq>Do you lift up your voice to the clouds, So that an abundance of water covers you?</dq> [35] <dq>Do you send out lightnings, and they go, And say to you, ‘Here we are!’?</dq> [36] <dq>Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the heart?</dq> [37] <dq>Who counts the clouds by wisdom? And who pours out the bottles of the heavens,</dq> [38] <dq>When the dust hardens in clumps, And the clods cleave together?</dq>

readings.title: The Provider of the Wild
readings.subtitle: Lions, Ravens, and Goats
readings.text: [Job 38:39] <dq>“Do you hunt the prey for the lion? Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,</dq> [40] <dq>When they bow down in the dens, And lie in wait in the lair?</dq> [41] <dq>Who provides food for the raven, When its young ones cry to <dn>El</dn>, And wander about for lack of food?</dq> [Job 39:1] <dq>“Do you know <dn>את</dn> the time the wild mountain goats bear young? Or do you mark when the hinds give birth?</dq> [2] <dq>Do you number the months they complete? Or do you know the time when they bear young?</dq> [3] <dq>They bow down, They bring forth their young, They cast out their labour pains.</dq> [4] <dq>Their young ones are healthy, They grow up with grain; They go out and do not return to them.</dq> [5] <dq>Who sent out the wild donkey free? And who loosened the bands of the wild donkey,</dq> [6] <dq>Whose home <dn>I</dn> have made the wilderness, And the barren land his dwelling?</dq> [7] <dq>He laughs at the turmoil of the city; He does not hear the shouting of the driver.</dq> [8] <dq>The range of mountains is his pasture, And he searches after every green thing.</dq> [9] <dq>Is the wild ox willing to serve you? Does he stay at your feeding-trough?</dq> [10] <dq>Do you bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes? Or does he plough the valleys behind you?</dq> [11] <dq>Do you trust him because his strength is great? Or do you leave your labour to him?</dq> [12] <dq>Do you trust him to bring home your grain, And gather it to your threshing-floor?</dq>

readings.title: The Fearless Horse and the Hawk
readings.subtitle: Majesty in Creation
readings.text: [Job 39:13] <dq>“The wing of the ostrich waves joyously, But are her wings and feathers like the stork’s?</dq> [14] <dq>“For she leaves her eggs on the earth, And warms them in the dust,</dq> [15] <dq>“And forgets that a foot might crush them, Or that a wild beast might trod them down.</dq> [16] <dq>“She treats her young harshly, as if not hers; Her toil is in vain, without fear;</dq> [17] <dq>“Because <dn>Eloah</dn> deprived her of wisdom, And did not give her a share of understanding.</dq> [18] <dq>“When she lifts herself on high, She laughs at the horse and his rider.</dq> [19] <dq>“Do you give the horse strength? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?</dq> [20] <dq>“Do you make him leap like a locust? The splendour of his snorting is awesome.</dq> [21] <dq>“He paws in the valley, and rejoices in strength; He goes out to meet the armour.</dq> [22] <dq>“He laughs at fear, and is not frightened; And he does not turn back from the sword.</dq> [23] <dq>“A quiver rattles against him, The glittering spear and javelin.</dq> [24] <dq>“With shaking and rage he swallows the ground, And does not believe that it is the sound of the shofar.</dq> [25] <dq>“At the blast of the shofar he says, ‘Aha!’ And from afar he smells the battle, The thunder of commanders and shouting.</dq> [26] <dq>“Does the hawk fly by your wisdom, And spread its wings toward the south?</dq> [27] <dq>“Does the eagle mount up at your command, And make its nest on high?</dq> [28] <dq>“It dwells on the rock, and stays, On the crag of the rock and the stronghold.</dq> [29] <dq>“From there it spies out the food; Its eyes see from afar.</dq> [30] <dq>“And its young ones suck up blood; And where the slain are, there it is!”</dq>

readings.title: The Challenger Humbled
readings.subtitle: Job's Silence
readings.text: [Job 40:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered <dn>את</dn> Job, and said, [2] <dq>“Is the reprover to contend with the <dn>Almighty</dn>? Let him who argues with <dn>Eloah</dn> answer it.”</dq> [3] And Job answered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, [4] “See, I am vile; what shall I answer <dn>You</dn>? I have laid my hand on my mouth. [5] “Once I have spoken, but I do not answer; And twice, but I add no more.”
